h1: The 6 Best Dehumidifiers Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six dehumidifiers under $300, compared on room coverage, tank size, drain hose options and features for bedrooms and basements.
summary: The AEOCKY is the biggest option, while the Kesnos 34 Pint is our best overall pick under $300, thanks to 2,000 square feet of coverage and a continuous drain hose. The KeepGlad suits bedrooms, the ToLife is the sleep-friendly pick, and the TABYIK adds closet boxes.
intro: Dehumidifier coverage claims are the easiest number to be misled by, because a 1,000 square foot rating assumes a moderately damp room and not a wet basement in August. The tank size matters just as much, since a small tank means emptying it every day.

We reviewed eight dehumidifiers and ranked six on the spec sheet: listed coverage, tank size, drain hose, timers and sleep modes. The 80-pint AEOCKY is listed in a higher bracket, so check its live price before buying.

products.name: AEOCKY 5500 Sq.Ft Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 Dehumidifier Max 80Pint/D
products.verdict: Energy Star certified with 5,500 square feet of listed coverage and 80 pints per day.
products.description:
The AEOCKY lists 5,500 square feet of coverage, Energy Star certification and a maximum capacity of 80 pints per day, far beyond the single-room models here. It is built for whole-house or large basement use.

It ranks first on capacity, but it sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, so confirm the current price is under $300 before you commit. The Kesnos below is cheaper and covers less.

Buy it for a big basement. The caveat is price and size: it is overkill for one bedroom.
products.skipIf: You only have a bedroom to dry.

products.name: Kesnos 34 Pin Dehumidifiers for Home and Basements, Dehumidifiers For Bedroom with Continuous Drain Hose For 2000 Sq. Ft, 24H Timer, Child Lock and Auto Defrost for Basement, Office and Bathroom
products.verdict: 2,000 square feet of coverage with a continuous drain hose and a 24-hour timer.
products.description:
The Kesnos lists 2,000 square feet of coverage, the largest here, plus a continuous drain hose, 24-hour timer, child lock and auto defrost. The hose means you can skip emptying the tank entirely.

It ranks second behind the AEOCKY, mainly because coverage and the continuous drain solve the two biggest annoyances of damp rooms. The 1,000 square foot models below are fine for bedrooms but not basements.

Buy it for a basement or large living area. The caveat is that continuous draining needs a spot near a floor drain or sink.
products.skipIf: You only need to dry a small bedroom.

products.name: KeepGlad Dehumidifier, 98OZ Dehumidifiers for Home(1000sq.ft), Humidity Display Dehumidifier for Basement Bathroom Bedroom, Auto Shut Off, Washable Filter, Drain Hose, Timer, 7 Ambient Lights, White
products.verdict: A 98 oz tank with a humidity display and washable filter for 1,000 square feet.
products.description:
The KeepGlad lists 1,000 square feet of coverage, a 98 oz tank, a humidity display, washable filter, drain hose and timer. The display lets you see the room humidity at a glance.

It ranks third because it covers fewer square feet than the Kesnos but adds the display. You trade coverage for monitoring.

Pick it for a bedroom or small apartment. The caveat is that a 1,000 square foot rating is not meant for a very wet space.

products.name: ToLife Dehumidifier, 1000 Sq Ft 95 oz Tank with Sleep Mode, Auto Shutoff
products.verdict: A 95 oz tank with a sleep mode and auto shutoff.
products.description:
The ToLife lists 1,000 square feet of coverage, a 95 oz tank, sleep mode and auto shutoff. The sleep mode is aimed at bedrooms where noise matters.

It ranks fourth because the listing is shorter than KeepGlad's, with no display or drain hose named. You gain a night-friendly mode.

Pick it for a light sleeper. The caveat is that the tank still needs emptying.

products.name: TABYIK Dehumidifiers for Home, 101oz Dehumidifier & 2pack Rechargeable Dehumidifying Boxes - Auto Shut Off Auto Defrost Quiet Dehumidifiers for Bathroom Room Wardrobe Closet Trailer RV
products.verdict: A 101 oz tank plus two rechargeable dehumidifying boxes.
products.description:
The TABYIK lists a 101 oz tank, auto shutoff and auto defrost, and bundles a two-pack of rechargeable dehumidifying boxes for closets.

It ranks fifth because the listing shows no coverage figure, so room fit is a guess. The extra boxes add closet protection.

Pick it for a bedroom plus closet. The caveat is the missing coverage rating.
products.skipIf: You need a stated coverage figure.

products.name: NineSky Dehumidifiers for Home, 1000 Sq.Ft Dehumidifier with 95oz Water Tank, Quiet Dehumidifier for Basement Bathroom Bedroom with 7-Color Ambient Light & Auto Shut Off, White
products.verdict: A 95 oz unit with a 7-colour ambient light.
products.description:
The NineSky lists 1,000 square feet of coverage, a 95 oz tank and a seven-colour ambient light.

It ranks sixth because the light is a gimmick next to the display and drain features on the KeepGlad. It suits those who like it.

Pick it for a nightstand. The caveat is that the light adds nothing to drying.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms where mood lighting is welcome.

whatMatters.detail: Coverage is the square footage a dehumidifier is rated for, and ratings assume moderate dampness. For wet spaces, pick one rated higher than the room. Check the sq ft number in the title.
Tank size sets how long before you must empty it. Ounces here range from 58 to 101. Check the number and use a drain hose if you hate emptying.
A hose lets water flow to a drain, so no tank emptying. It needs a nearby drain or sink. Look for the words drain hose in the bullets.
Auto shutoff stops the unit when the tank is full, and defrost prevents ice. Both protect the machine. Check for them in the listing.
Noise matters in bedrooms. Sleep modes help, but few listings show decibels. Look for a numeric figure before trusting a quiet claim.

faq.q: What size dehumidifier do I need?
faq.a: Match the listed coverage to your room, and go higher for damp spaces.
Buying a small unit for a wet basement. It will run constantly.

faq.q: Is the Kesnos worth it over the KeepGlad?
faq.a: Yes for large or wet spaces. For bedrooms, the KeepGlad is enough.

faq.q: How do I use a drain hose?
faq.a: Connect the hose and run it downhill to a drain or sink.
Wash the filter and empty the tank regularly.
Models with auto shutoff are designed to stop when the tank is full.

finalTake: The Kesnos is the dehumidifier under $300 most people with damp rooms should buy. The KeepGlad suits bedrooms, the ToLife suits light sleepers, and the 58 oz mini handles closets. Match coverage to the room and you are set.
